paper.title: Voyager: An Open-Ended Embodied Agent with Large Language Models
paper.central_claim: Voyager, an LLM-powered embodied lifelong-learning agent in Minecraft, combines an automatic curriculum, an ever-growing skill library of executable code and iterative prompting with environment feedback, execution errors and self-verification; without parameter updates it obtains 3.3x more unique items, travels 2.3x longer and unlocks tech-tree milestones up to 15.3x faster than prior SOTA, and reuses the learned library to solve novel tasks in a new world.
paper.scope_decision: in_scope (borderline): frozen GPT-4 harness (code-as-action over Mineflayer control primitives, critic-gated skill library, LLM curriculum) controlling a simulated 3D Minecraft avatar that navigates and interacts; perception and sensorimotor control are delegated to the high-level API and excluded by the authors. Consistent with DEPS (2302.01560) and the VirtualHome/ALFWorld symbolic-action precedents; the 2606.12372 out_of_scope precedent does not apply. Claims and ratings are limited to symbolic high-level game control.

preliminary_judgment: Written after reading the fixed text, before opening this paper's seat records: system_method; 3 trials per method; items and tech-tree fractions out of 3 from inventory/environment state with +-sd on iterations; same GPT-4 and 160-iteration cap for author-adapted ReAct/Reflexion/AutoGPT; one-at-a-time ablations of curriculum, library, three feedback types and GPT-4 (text percentages, curves figure-only); new-world test of 4 unseen tasks x 3 attempts where the no-library variant already solves 11/12, so the library's held-out effect is mostly efficiency; the GPT-4 critic gates skill admission without a false-positive audit; high-level API with no perception; bot resurrected with inventory preserved. Scope borderline-in (DEPS precedent). Expected online (same game/avatar/task family), scoped; M/X strong, E moderate to good, cost unpriced.

signatures.object: an LLM-driven code-as-action loop in Minecraft: curriculum agent proposes a task, action agent writes Mineflayer JavaScript, critic agent verifies
signatures.information: text agent state (inventory, equipment, nearby blocks/entities, biome, time, health, position), chat-log environment feedback, interpreter errors, critic critique, top-5 retrieved skills; no pixels
signatures.operation: propose -> retrieve -> generate code -> execute -> feedback (errors, chat log, critic) -> regenerate up to 4 rounds
signatures.output: executable JavaScript skill and task outcome
signatures.conditions: GPT-4 code quality, high-level control API, tasks verifiable from player state
signatures.feedback: environment chat log, execution errors, GPT-4 critic success/critique
signatures.selection_rule_or_data: accept when the GPT-4 critic returns success; give up after 4 rounds and mark task failed
signatures.persistence: skill library (vector DB: embedding of GPT-3.5 description -> program), completed/failed task lists
signatures.later_use: top-5 skills retrieved by embedding of task plan + environment feedback for every later task and in the new world
signatures.claimed_effect: 3.3x unique items, 2.3x distance, 15.3x/8.5x/6.4x faster tech-tree milestones; solves four unseen tasks in a new world in 3/3 runs
signatures.failure_boundary: critic false negatives, curriculum hallucination, GPT-4 cost, no visual perception

signatures.object: automatic curriculum (GPT-4 proposes the next task from progress + state, GPT-3.5 self-asks/answers questions)
signatures.information: state, completed and failed task lists, optional wiki retrieval
signatures.operation: LLM-generated bottom-up task stream maximizing diversity
signatures.conditions: warm-up schedule releases state fields gradually
signatures.selection_rule_or_data: tasks must be verifiable from player status
signatures.claimed_effect: random curriculum loses 93% of discovered items

gap.author_gap: Prior LLM agents (ReAct, Reflexion, AutoGPT, Inner Monologue, CaP) and RL/IL agents do not accumulate, update and transfer skills over long horizons in an open-ended world.
gap.checked_gap: In the re-implemented baselines, ReAct/Reflexion make almost no progress (0/3 on every tech-tree level) and AutoGPT stalls before diamond; Voyager without the library also plateaus. The re-implementations are authored by the Voyager team and are not independent published Minecraft agents (DEPS, Plan4MC, DECKARD are tabulated but not run).
lineage: CaP / ProgPrompt (code as policy) + ReAct / Reflexion (feedback loops) + AutoGPT (task decomposition) -> Voyager (curriculum + verified skill library + iterative prompting)
Minecraft low-level controllers (VPT, DreamerV3) are orthogonal; high-level planners (DEPS, Plan4MC, DECKARD) are the nearest Minecraft lineage

closest_adjacent.name: DEPS / Plan4MC / DECKARD
closest_adjacent.unsolved_per_authors: no automatic curriculum, skill library or iterative planning (Table A.2)

gap.residue: No ablation against an independently implemented Minecraft LLM planner; the benefit of the library versus GPT-4's own Minecraft knowledge is not isolated.
gap.stakes: Gradient-free lifelong skill accumulation by a black-box LLM; relevance to robots is asserted, not shown.
gap.method_response: Add a self-proposed curriculum, a verified code skill library, and feedback-driven code repair.
gap.remaining_gap: GPT-4 cost, critic/curriculum errors, no visual perception (authors); no embodied-robot evidence, only 3 trials per cell (ours).
gap.unresolved: Neighbour papers not pinned; whether DEPS-class planners would close the gap is unknown.
gap.aggregate_note: son55 gap retained (neighbours tested vs only tabulated; GPT-4 prior knowledge not isolated). Added: the robotics residual is excluded by design (agg:E002), so stakes are credited only for LLM-agent lifelong skill accumulation in a game.

expectations.requirement: Hold the frontier backbone fixed and compare the proposed harness with at least one alternative harness or loop organization on the same episodes. For zero-shot VLN-CE the alternative is a rerun of a published zero-shot harness or workflow (2606.10577#s4, 2609.15195#s4) with the same model; for coding agents, a second deployable harness.

expectations.reason: ReAct, Reflexion and AutoGPT run with the same GPT-4 and iteration caps, but as author adaptations of NLP agents, not independently published Minecraft harnesses.

expectations.source_strength: ablation, common_practice; literature-derived, not an actual reviewer quotation
expectations.requirement: Attribute a gain to a harness component only through one-at-a-time toggles (leave-one-out or single add) with the backbone fixed. A cumulative stack (A, then +B, then +C) or a bundle-level comparison does not separate components or their interactions.
expectations.applies_when: a claim that a specific harness component (depth tool, memory, verifier, skill library, plugin, feedback channel) causes the improvement.
expectations.reason: Curriculum, library, environment feedback, execution errors, self-verification and the code backbone are each ablated one at a time with the rest fixed.

expectations.source_strength: ablation, common_practice; literature-derived, not an actual reviewer quotation
expectations.requirement: Report the harness or tool effect under at least two backbones of different strength. Several read papers find that tools and imposed structure help weak models and are neutral or harmful for strong ones. A gain measured on the teacher therefore does not predict the gain for a compact student.
expectations.applies_when: a claim that a harness component or tool helps in general, or that a teacher-measured tool value will carry to a student.
expectations.reason: The harness-vs-baseline gap is never measured under a second backbone: GPT-3.5 replaces GPT-4 only inside Voyager's code generation (a within-harness ablation), and 0314 vs 0613 are snapshots of one model, not two strengths.
expectations.aggregate_reason: Both seats said partial (shared correction SEC-1); score item set to E.causality (son55) instead of sol's E.holdout.

A single run on a 100-episode subset is treated as descriptive. In the read single-run papers, differences of a few points sit within noise.

expectations.reason: GPT-4 price ratio acknowledged; calls, tokens, latency and dollars per iteration are not reported.

claims.text: Voyager obtains 3.3x more unique items, travels 2.3x longer and reaches tech-tree milestones up to 15.3x faster than prior SOTA.
claims.setting: MineDojo/Mineflayer, GPT-4-0314, 160 prompting iterations, 3 runs per method
claims.baseline_control: ReAct, Reflexion, AutoGPT re-implemented by the authors with the same GPT-4 and feedback channels
claims.selection_vs_test: no separate selection split; metric is count of unique inventory items and iteration to milestone
claims.result_denominator: 63 unique items in 160 iterations; milestones in 3/3 runs up to iron, diamond 1/3 (102 iterations); baselines 0/3 (ReAct, Reflexion) and no diamond (AutoGPT)
claims.allowed_conclusion: Against three authors-adapted NLP agents, the full harness progresses much further in a 3-run Minecraft exploration benchmark; 'prior SOTA' is not an independent Minecraft agent.

claims.text: The learned skill library lets Voyager solve novel tasks in a new world from scratch, and also helps other methods.
claims.setting: new Minecraft world, four unseen tasks (diamond pickaxe, golden sword, lava bucket, compass), 50 iterations, 3 attempts
claims.baseline_control: ReAct, Reflexion, AutoGPT, AutoGPT with Voyager's library, Voyager without library
claims.selection_vs_test: fresh world and empty inventory; library from earlier lifelong learning (which run unspecified)
claims.result_denominator: Voyager 3/3 on all four; w/o library 2/3, 3/3, 3/3, 3/3; AutoGPT+library 1/3, 1/3, 0/3, 2/3; others 0/3
claims.allowed_conclusion: Within Minecraft, retrieved verified skills speed up and rescue unseen tech-tree tasks over 3 attempts; 'w/o library' still succeeds in 11/12 attempts so the margin is in iterations.

assessment.evidence_level_reason: Closed-loop Minecraft runs scored from environment state with run counts. The new-world test applies a library built in another world, which a literal reading of the EVIDENCE transfer clause ("scene sets not used when building skills/memory") could count; it is held at online because it is the same simulator, avatar and task family, the prompts/APIs/curriculum rules were developed on Minecraft, and only 4 tasks x 3 attempts are run. This matches the p002 reading that benchmark-internal held-out splits are online; flagged for controller confirmation (evidence_level is unscored).
assessment.author_claim_preserved: Voyager is the first LLM-powered embodied lifelong learning agent; it obtains 3.3x more unique items, travels 2.3x longer and unlocks tech-tree milestones up to 15.3x faster than prior SOTA, and uses its learned skill library to solve novel tasks in a new world while other techniques struggle to generalize.
assessment.strongest_supported_claim: In a 3-run Minecraft study with GPT-4 over the high-level Mineflayer API (no perception, no motor control), curriculum + critic-gated executable skill library + execution-feedback repair discovers far more items and reaches tech-tree levels far sooner than author-adapted ReAct/Reflexion/AutoGPT under the same prompting-iteration cap. One-at-a-time ablations support each component on the discovered-item metric, and in a fresh world the stored library lets Voyager solve four unseen tool tasks in 3/3 attempts with fewer iterations than without it (the no-library variant still solves 11/12).

G.reason: Both seats 3; confirmed. Specific bottleneck (LLM agents do not accumulate, reuse and transfer skills over long horizons; one-shot code generation fails) with a clear lineage (CaP/ProgPrompt, ReAct/Reflexion, AutoGPT, Minecraft planners). Not 4: the strongest Minecraft neighbours (DEPS, Plan4MC, DECKARD) are only tabulated, the baseline failure diagnosis rests on the authors' re-implementations of NLP agents, and the residual for embodied robotics (perception, sensorimotor control) is excluded by design (agg:E002).

M.reason: Resolved toward son55 (sol 3). Each of the three operations targets a named failure and makes a distinguishable prediction that is tested in the main domain with GPT-4 fixed: random/manual vs automatic curriculum, library removal, removal of each feedback type, GPT-3.5 swap. Information conditions (text player state, no vision), the selection rule (critic success after <=4 rounds) and persistence (description-embedding-keyed library, top-5 retrieval) are reconstructible, and the curriculum is constrained to tasks verifiable from player state, which grounds the critic assumption by construction. sol's limits (uncalibrated admission, privileged executor) are evidence and scope issues scored in E; they do not make the mechanism's logic weak. The untested forgetting claim is handled in claim_support.

X.reason: Resolved toward sol (son55 4). Prompts, API list, pseudo-code, round cap, top-5 retrieval, temperatures and warm-up schedule are given, so the static loop is rebuildable. Not 4 because the retention chain has unstated conditions that the X anchor names: how duplicate or conflicting skills are handled when a new program is added, which lifelong run supplies the library used in the new-world test, and what a "prompting iteration" counts when curriculum, critic, GPT-3.5 helpers and embeddings are also called. Environment affordances (resurrection with inventory preserved, recycling of crafting table/furnace, agg:E001) are further unstated applicability conditions; robotics applicability is asserted without a boundary (agg:E006).

measurement.reason: Resolved toward son55 (sol 2). Headline results are environment-state measurements: unique items from inventory (per-trial item lists in App B.4.1), tech-tree levels and new-world tasks as success fractions out of 3 runs with mean+-sd iterations. sol's cap rests on the unaudited self-verification, but the critic only gates skill admission; it is not the measurement instrument for items, tech-tree levels or task success. Not 4: 3 runs only, ablation magnitudes are text percentages over figure-only curves, map distance is figure-only, and the bot is resurrected with inventory preserved (agg:E001), so "unique items in 160 iterations" is not a standard MineDojo task protocol.

causality.reason: Both seats 3; confirmed. Same GPT-4 and the same 160/50 prompting-iteration caps for author-adapted ReAct/Reflexion/AutoGPT, plus one-at-a-time ablations of curriculum, library, environment feedback, execution errors, self-verification and the code-generation backbone, and the library transplanted into AutoGPT. Not 4: baselines are re-implementations of NLP agents rather than Minecraft planners, per-iteration model calls are unequal, GPT-4's prior Minecraft knowledge is not controlled (son55:E030), and no harness-vs-baseline contrast is run under a second backbone (E03).

holdout.reason: Resolved toward son55 (sol 2). The new-world test uses a library built in a different world, an emptied inventory and four target items that do not appear in the lifelong runs' item lists, and the library effect is kept there (19/18/21/18 vs 36/30/27/26 iterations; diamond pickaxe 3/3 vs 2/3; AutoGPT 0/3 -> some successes with the library). That is more than the anchor-2 case (development overlap or held-out gain about 0). Not 4: same simulator, avatar and task family, 4 tasks x 3 attempts, library provenance unstated, GPT-4 also decomposes the task into subgoals (agg:E005), and without the library Voyager still solves 11/12, so the held-out benefit of the memory is mostly efficiency.

statistics.reason: Resolved toward son55 (sol 3). Three runs per cell with +-sd on iteration counts, fractions out of 3 and a 309-sample retrieval audit with +-; but no CI or paired test, N=3, and failures (critic misses, hallucinated tasks/fuel, stuck rounds) are qualitative only. Anchor v2 precedent (2209.11302): variance present but no CI and no failure decomposition -> 2, not 3.

cost.reason: Both seats 2; confirmed. Budgets are equalised only as prompting-iteration caps and the GPT-4 price ratio is acknowledged; tokens, calls per iteration (curriculum, critic, GPT-3.5 helpers, embeddings), latency and dollars are not reported. Anchor: call budget inferable but not priced -> 2.

resolutions.reason: C03 explicitly includes a sub-move that skips upstream tuning and conditions the frozen model on retrieved reference instances, which is what top-5 skill retrieval does. son55's premise that C03 needs an upstream tuning phase overlooks this. Fit stays partial (no category holdout).
See ratings.M: every operation has a distinguishable prediction tested in the main domain; sol's limits belong in E and scope.

See ratings.X: retention-chain conditions (dedup/conflict policy, library provenance for the new-world test, iteration accounting) and environment affordances are unstated; son55 itself lists the first two as gaps.
Metrics come from inventory/environment state with explicit run denominators; the critic is not the measuring instrument, so sol's cap ground does not apply. Small N and figure-only curves prevent 4.
Fresh world, empty inventory, unseen items and a library built elsewhere, with the library gain kept; better than the anchor-2 overlap case but small and within one game.
Variance present, no CI/paired test, failures only qualitative: anchor v2 precedent 2209.11302 gives 2.

resolutions.reason: EVIDENCE harness definition is met (frozen frontier LLM; control-primitive tools; skill library; verifier; execution control) and the object is a simulated 3D embodied avatar that navigates and interacts. Precedents: DEPS 2302.01560 (Minecraft) and the VirtualHome/ALFWorld symbolic-action papers are in scope. The 2606.12372 out_of_scope precedent needs no frontier LLM, a human teacher or a learned intervention module; none of these holds. The authors' exclusion of perception and sensorimotor control (agg:E002) limits G stakes and claim scope; it is not grounds for exclusion.
